belief: I'll always be behind everyone else.
origins: Being the last to finish, needing extra help, or taking longer can make us feel in a permanent race we cannot win. Comparison drains energy and joy.
teaches: “Let us run with endurance the race set out for us” (Hebrews 12:1). It is our race, not someone else’s. “The race is not to the swift” (Ecclesiastes 9:11). “Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.” Each person has a different path and pace. God is concerned with faithfulness, not speed, and He rejoices in your steps.
errors: Believing I am either ahead or behind.
Predicting that I will never catch up.
Feeling slow and concluding I am behind in life.
questions: Who am I comparing myself to, and why?
What progress have I made compared with myself last year?
What areas am I not behind in?
What is a reasonable pace for me?
What does Scripture say about running my own race?
Whom can I walk with at my pace?
truth: I am running my own race, at my own pace, with God’s help. Progress matters more than comparison, and faithfulness matters more than speed.
hw_truths: The race is not just to the swift.
log: Each week, note one improvement from last month.
actions: Write one thing better than last year.
Walk with someone at your pace.
prayer: Lord, I feel behind. Help me run my race at my pace, grateful for progress, and free from comparison. Amen.
